land.text: the Zirid coast: Mahdia, Sousse and Sfax, taken in 1148; Tripoli taken in 1146

predecessors.note: The page gives the emir as al-Hasan ibn Ali, who fled Mahdia on 22 June 1148 'leaving their treasure behind'.

land.text: the Norman towns of coastal Ifriqiya: Gabes taken 'by force' and Mahdia 'breached' in January 1160, Tripoli recognising Almohad authority

successors.note: A final Siculo-Almohad peace was signed only in 1180.

capitals.name: Tripoli
capitals.note: The page gives no seat for the Norman holdings; Tripoli was the first mainland conquest ('In 1146 he successfully besieged it').

capitals.name: Mahdia
capitals.note: Not stated as a capital by the page: it is the Zirid capital the Normans took on 22 June 1148, the base of 'Philip of Mahdia' (1152) and the last Norman holdout; the kingdom was ruled from Palermo.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1146-1147: Cliopatria's row starts in 1152. The page: 'conquests of mainland Africa started between 1146-1148'; Tripoli was besieged successfully in 1146 (a first try failed in '1142/3'). Djerba (taken 1135) is an island too small for the grid and is left out.

New keyframe for 1148-1151: Mahdia (22 June), Sousse (1 July) and Sfax (12 July) added to Tripoli. Gabes is not included: the page has it 'taken by force' only during the Almohad siege of 1159-1160 and gives no Norman conquest date.

correction.text: the coast from Tripoli to the borders of Tunis, without Tunis

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 39,613 km2 coastal belt (135 cells: 103 Tunisian, 32 Libyan) holds 1152-1157 here, not to 1168. It includes Tunis (13 cells), which the page treats as a tributary, not a possession ('the kings of Tunis paid him tribute'; 'the dominion of the Franks extended from Tripoli to the borders of Tunis'; Houben: 'a constellation of Norman-held towns along coastal Ifriqiya'), so the correction removes it. The page has no infobox, so no area comparison is possible.

New keyframe for 1158-1160 (Cliopatria has the full belt to 1168, which is wrong): 'Tripoli fell in 1158'; 'All of Norman Africa was essentially abandoned to the Almohads save Mahdia'; Mahdia 'under siege from late in the summer of 1159' and breached in January 1160. After 1160 nothing is Norman: the Almohad page has Mahdia surrender in January 1160.

ledger.note: 1146: Roger II's Sicilians take Tripoli, the first mainland foothold of the Norman Kingdom of Africa. 'While the island of Djerba was conquered by Roger II in 1135, conquests of mainland Africa started between 1146-1148'; of Tripoli: 'In 1146 he successfully besieged it' (a first attempt failed in '1142/3'). The page does not name the ruler of Tripoli; the Zirid dossier records the end of Zirid overlordship here.

1148: Tunis pays tribute to Roger II. Bridging the year: the page says 'the kings of Tunis paid him [Roger] tribute' (Andrea Dandolo) and that the Tunisians 'sent grain to Sicily in hopes of averting an attack', with no date; Roger died in 1154 and 'was still in power in Tunis when the Almohads attacked in 1159' (Ibn Idhari).
22 June 1148: George of Antioch's fleet takes Mahdia, the Zirid capital. 'When the Sicilians reached Mahdia on 22 June, the emir and his court fled the unprepared city leaving their treasure behind.'
1 July 1148: Sousse surrenders without a fight. 'On 1 July the city of Sousse (Susa) ... surrendered without a fight'; the year comes from the page's 1148 narrative.
12 July 1148: Sfax falls after a short resistance. 'On 12 July Sfax fell after a short resistance'; the year comes from the page's 1148 narrative.

1158: Tripoli rebels and is lost. 'Tripoli fell in 1158'; the Almohad page says Tripoli 'rebelled against the Normans two years earlier' than January 1160. The rebel city has no state of its own, hence 'nobody' until it recognises Almohad authority in 1160.

1158-1159: the Norman towns of the coast are abandoned to the Almohads except Mahdia. 'All of Norman Africa was essentially abandoned to the Almohads save Mahdia'; Gabes 'was taken by force' in the siege of 1159-1160. The year is the page's range; the region (Sousse and Sfax, with Gabes) is the researcher's reading.

1159: the Almohads attack Tunis and end its tribute to Sicily. 'The Almohads ... attacked it in 1159' (the Almohad page: Abd al-Mu'min took Tunis in 1159); the Kingdom of Africa page says Tunis was not itself taken by the Normans.

January 1160: Mahdia falls and the Norman Kingdom of Africa ends. 'Mahdia was besieged soon after and surrendered in January 1160' (Almohad page); the Kingdom of Africa page: 'Mahdia was under siege from late in the summer of 1159' and 'In January 1160 Mahdia was breached'.

wars.name: Sicilian conquest of Zirid Ifriqiya
wars.outcome: Norman victory: Tripoli 1146, then Mahdia 22 June, Sousse 1 July and Sfax 12 July 1148.
wars.note: Roger II conquered Djerba in 1135 ('his first permanent conquest').

wars.name: Almohad conquest of Norman Africa

zones.text: the Norman coast, Mahdia and Tunis

wars.outcome: Almohad victory: Tripoli lost in 1158, Mahdia under siege from late summer 1159 and breached in January 1160; a final peace with the Almohads came only in 1180.
wars.note: The page calls the fall of the kingdom 'the Almohad Caliphate (1158-1160)'.

certainty.note: A string of coastal towns, not a bordered territory: no page gives a frontier, and the Houben quote on the page calls it 'a constellation of Norman-held towns'.

sources.title: Kingdom of Africa
sources.note: Identity, conquest dates 1146-1148, Tripoli 1158, Mahdia 1159-1160, tribute of Tunis, the 1180 peace; no infobox in the text read (no area).

sources.title: Almohad Caliphate
sources.note: Mahdia 'surrendered in January 1160' and Tripoli 'recognized Almohad authority right after'; Tunis March 1159.

notes: CLIOPATRIA. The row is 1152-1168; the page supports 1146-1160. The shape includes Tunis, which was only a tributary. Years 1161-1168 are Almohad: see almohad-caliphate (its 1152 and 1169 shapes carry the Norman coast from 1159-1160). NOT SETTLED. The ruler of Tripoli in 1146; who held Gabes before the Normans and when they took it; the fate of Bone (the page only has a fleet 'sent to conquer Bone' in 1152); whether Mahdia was ever a capital. The infobox was absent from the text read, so the Cliopatria area (39,613 km2) is uncompared. Djerba (1135) is outside the dossier's life and too small for the grid. COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT A DOSSIER: 'Banu Khurasan (Tunis)' (Tunis ruled by a local dynasty, tributary to Sicily); Tripoli's rebel regime of 1158-1160 is recorded as 'nobody'. The Norman king (Roger II to 1154, then William I) rules from Palermo: the metropole is kingdom-of-sicily (Cliopatria 1139-1384), which should record this colony as a vassal tint.
